I was getting excited about this and what they claimed they offered through their service.  Then it asked me to pay what I could and it ranged from $1 to $19 and some change.  I only answered the questions regarding ADHD so far so until I was more informed about the services they provide, I chose $1 for the time being.  It then asked me if I wanted to get some type of guide for $14.99 I think..not 100% sure word for word but I do know it was close to that and around $15.  I declined as I have no idea what that entailed.  Then I was made aware of the app behind this brand and I could go download it, and it would provide my test results from the ADHD quiz on the app and some brain games, some skills to help that were helpful to people like me.  There was a download button.  I clicked on that and went to download the app from the App Store. Next thing i get a push notification saying that I was being charged $14.99 from the Breeze App.  

Now im so turned off by this, although I was eager to check it out, I would rather find something else and I want to warn others that this practice they follow should be banned by the App Store.  I don’t know if everyone in that company is aware but that’s deceptive and it’s not authorized to charge when you ask to download an app and don’t make any costs known up front.  I hope you charge it, I don’t think you would appreciate the dishonest way it goes about if it were you just checking out a new app.

reviews.title: BEWARE SCAMMERS
reviews.text:
I discovered I had been paying $29.99/month for several months without realizing I had an active recurring subscription. On August 18, I contacted Breeze through the app to cancel and asked for a refund of my most recent charge. They denied the refund, but confirmed in writing that my subscription was canceled and that there would be “no future renewals or charges.”

Then I was charged another $29.99 on August 24.

When I complained, Breeze claimed the charge was actually initiated at 1:09 AM on August 19 and that my cancellation wasn’t processed until 2:03 AM. They are using that technicality to refuse my refund—even though I had already contacted them to cancel and they explicitly told me there would be no future charges.

I’m not asking for the previous months of charges. I’m asking for the ONE charge that occurred after they confirmed my cancellation.

I’ve filed a BBB complaint and am sharing this because other customers deserve to know how their cancellation and billing practices are handled. Breeze, refund the $29.99 you charged me after confirming my cancellation.

reviews.title: Misleading Charges
reviews.text:
I signed up for what I understood to be a low-cost 7-day trial. During that process, I was also charged $19.99 for an “optional” mental wellbeing guide, followed by a $29.99 subscription renewal at the end of the trial period. In total, nearly $50 in charges were associated with a 7-day trial experience.

When I contacted Breeze, they explained that the $19.99 charge was a separate add-on and that the $29.99 was the monthly subscription renewal. I requested refunds for both charges and escalated the issue, but Breeze refused to refund either one.

Regardless of what may technically be disclosed during checkout, the overall billing structure felt confusing, overly aggressive, and not transparent enough from a consumer standpoint. I would never have knowingly agreed to pay nearly $50 for one week of access.

The subscription has now been canceled, but I’ve disputed the charges with my card issuer. I strongly recommend reading every checkout screen extremely carefully before entering any payment information.

reviews.title: Great App - Change or Get Rid of Subscription Model
reviews.text:
The app itself might actually be worth the subscription—the way they sell the subscription is my issue.

I initially downloaded Breeze for my assessment results and then, ironically, forgot about the app until I saw the subscription charge. But when I finally opened it and looked at my daily plan, I was genuinely impressed. The tasks were simple, realistic, and actually felt achievable—things like focusing on one task for 25 minutes, making the bed, or remembering basic self-care. For someone struggling with mental health, ADHD, or executive functioning, sometimes those “small” things aren’t small at all.

My issue is the automatic-renewal model. An app designed for people who may struggle with forgetfulness and executive functioning probably shouldn’t rely on those same people remembering to cancel a subscription. I also found that a significantly lower price was offered when I tried to cancel, which made me wish the pricing had simply been more transparent and flexible from the beginning.

Don’t let the subscription model discourage you from trying the app, because I genuinely like what I’ve seen so far. But I would encourage other users to contact Breeze and ask for non-renewing options—maybe a small one-time fee for assessment results, a paid 7–14 day trial that simply ENDS, or a month of access that requires you to actively choose to renew.

Give people a chance to experience the value first, then let us consciously choose to keep paying for it.

Great concept. Useful app. I just hope Breeze develops a subscription model that’s as thoughtful as the product itself.

reviews.title: NO ETHICS, NO VALUES — THE IRONY IS UNBELIEVABLE
reviews.text: The irony is unbelievable. This is an app that supposedly promotes self-discovery, emotional wellness, reducing stress, and becoming a better version of yourself, yet my experience with their customer service showed the complete opposite. I have proof that I tried to cancel during the trial. A simple typo in the registration email caused the cancellation not to match the account, and even after this was explained—and despite me not using the app afterward—they still refused to refund me. How can you sell wellness, personal growth, and doing better while treating your own customers this way? Practice what you preach. Zero values, zero ethics, and absolutely not worth doing business with.
